_what: The provenance record for every third-party asset the arena's Tier 2 figure library is built from (report 13 §9.1, §9.2). tools/build-figures.mjs reads it, VERIFIES every source archive against the sha256 and byte count below before it builds anything, extracts the members it needs from the verified archives itself, builds web/public/models/figures.glb, and WRITES web/src/arena/figures/models.json from what it measured — so the manifest is the hand-written half (where a file came from, what its licence badge said on the day) and models.json is the measured half (heights, widths, bones, triangles, the clip names that really exist, and the built file's own sha256).
_licence_rule: Only CC0 assets are used at all (user decision). The badge text below is what the download page said ON THE DAY, verbatim, because that is the only evidence that survives the page changing — Quaternius relicensed one of its 83 packs sixteen days before slice 1 (report 12 §0.2), and QAL §7 says the version in force when you obtained the asset governs.
_never: Nothing derived from card art may ever appear here, nothing from Mixamo (D54), and no AI-generated mesh. Marvel art is licensed to Wizards; the Fan Content Policy's line is "If you don't have the rights to use another person's stuff in your Fan Content—don't" (https://company.wizards.com/en/legal/fancontentpolicy). NOTICE §2 and the Scryfall images already live under that rule.
_where: The downloaded archives are NOT committed. They live under var/assets/figures/ (var/ is gitignored) exactly as downloaded — a zip is NOT unzipped by hand any more: the build reads the member it needs out of the verified zip. Re-download with the URLs below; the build refuses a file whose sha256 or byte count differs, and prints the URL.
_reverified: 2026-09-27 (slice 2): all three slice-1 sources were re-downloaded from the URLs below into a fresh worktree and matched their recorded sha256 and byte count exactly; the three badges were re-read and are unchanged. The Universal Animation Library is new on that date. 2026-09-27 (slice 4): all four were downloaded AGAIN into the tier2-slice4 worktree — the three direct links by curl, the Animation Library through itch.io's free-download flow — and all four matched byte for byte (`node tools/build-figures.mjs --verify-only`); rebuilt with slice 3's manifest, figures.glb came out byte-identical to the committed one (143,920 B, sha256 c09ac552…a981a3), which closes slice 3's follow-up 7. The Universal Base Characters are new on that date.

budget._what: Lane BODIES (D145), 2026-09-28: the byte budget of web/public/models/figures.glb, re-set by MEASUREMENT from report 13 §8.2's 400 kB (409,600 B, which the build typed in until this lane). tools/build-figures.mjs fails a build over either number and web/test/figures.test.ts holds the committed file to both. 450 KiB = 460,800 B.

measured.on: the committed figures.glb (373,236 B, sha256 fe13b02c…7aae90), read by a scratch GLB parser, 2026-09-28

budget._why: Two thirds of the file is its JSON chunk, and most of that is one accessor, sampler and channel record per animated joint per clip: a clip on the proportioned rig costs ~8.4 kB of JSON per body (23 channels) and under 1 kB of meshopt binary. So a new clip for both bodies is ~18 kB, and slice 4's 27 kB of headroom held ONE. What this lane's own plan would add with the Universal Base Characters pack (PLAN.md's lane-BODIES follow-ups): the pack's six other hairstyles as static nodes at ≤ 500 triangles (~7.7 B a triangle plus ~0.8 kB of JSON each: ~28 kB), its eye and two eyebrow meshes (~5 kB), and two more library clips for resting poses the table in figures/rests.ts cannot aim from the twelve it has (~36 kB) — ~69 kB, to ~442 kB. 450 KiB keeps ~18 kB over that. The triangle line stays report 13 §8.2's 30,000.
budget._cheaper: Not done here, and the cheaper road to headroom: the JSON's per-channel records could be halved by merging each body's clips into one long clip with named ranges (the clip lane already scrubs `action.time`), which the build would have to own.

ubc._what: Slice 4 — THE humanoid rig. The Universal Base Characters are on the Universal Animation Library's own 65-joint humanoid rig (same author, same joint names — the build asserts every body on this rig has EXACTLY the library mannequin's joint list), so the library's clips are carried onto them joint for joint by a world-space delta over the major skeleton, with no 7-joint chibi in between — which is what face-planted the head in slice 2 (D68). The fingers are not driven. Every clip below is the library's; nothing here is Mixamo.
ubc.joints: the clip library's own (asserted by the build against UAL1_Standard.glb's skin)

retarget._joints: Parents first. Each is driven by its source bone's world-space rotation away from the T-pose, carried onto this body's T-pose (the two rigs' rest orientations differ by up to 23° at the neck, measured, so local rotations are NOT copied). The fingers and `root` hold their bind.
retarget._upper: A clip written `ual:A+B` is COMPOSED: A's legs and hips under B's `upper` joints — the spine, the arms and the head — each retargeted first, then merged track by track, B sampled at A's frame times and looped. A's hips keep their pitch and roll (the legs are posed against them) but lose their TURN about the vertical, because Fixing_Kneeling turns its hips 40-odd degrees to work at the ground: a kneel on those hips turned Coulson's chest and Peggy's shield edge-on to the table camera (measured by traits.test.ts's raster: 1 px of tie, 6 px of shield), and a kneel on the idle's hips instead stood the figure up on one bent leg. The library has no kneel with an upright torso; `Fixing_Kneeling+Idle_Loop` is one.

hip._hip: The pelvis alone translates: by the source's world-space hip delta, scaled by the two hip heights.

ubc._clips: THE CHOICE, judged from lab renders of every candidate on the man's and the woman's bodies (docs/evidence/m7-tier2-slice4.md): the library's clips land on these bodies with no face-plant — the same rig, retargeted by world-space delta — so every clip is the library's own. `crouch` (a TAPPED creature's resting stance, held at 0.85) is COMPOSED: Fixing_Kneeling's legs under Idle_Loop's upright torso — a figure taking a knee, its chest (Coulson's badge and shirt) still facing the table, where the library's Crouch_Idle_Loop hunches it face-down. `shrink` keeps the hunch (Ant-Man's attack, Quantum Reduction's host), `block` is Sword_Idle's guard with no sword, `summon` is the landing of a jump, and Agent 13's `pistolDraw` is Pistol_Shoot's two-handed aim.

kenney-mini._what: THE humanoid rig. Every humanoid archetype (agent, hero, scientist) is a Kenney Mini character, and all twelve of those share this rig exactly — so every humanoid shares ONE clip set, written once here and baked into each model by the build. The build asserts that every model naming this rig has exactly these joints.

retarget._what: Report 13 §9.5's experiment: SkeletonUtils.retargetClip from the Universal Animation Library onto this rig, run offline by the build (three in Node), so the browser never ships the 7.6 MB source rig. A clip written 'ual:<name>' below is one of these; every other clip is the pack's own.
retarget._names: Both rigs are T-posed and face +Z with their left side at +x (measured), so a joint's WORLD rotation delta from its bind pose transfers directly; localOffsets = inverse(sourceBind) × targetBind is what makes the two joint-axis conventions agree. The chibi has no elbows, knees, clavicles or neck, so the upper arm, the thigh and the chest carry the whole limb.

hip._hip: The chibi's root is at its FEET and its legs and torso hang from it, where the source's pelvis is at its hips; so the root takes the pelvis's TRANSLATION only (scaled by hip height, 0.176 / 0.917) and never its rotation — a rotating root would swing both legs about the ground point.

kenney-mini._clips: THE DECISION, measured in docs/evidence/m7-tier2-slice2.md (the figures section, §3; var/shots-t8/clips-compare.png): retargeted onto a 7-joint chibi, the library's HIT and DEATH read — and supply the two clips the pack does not have (slice 1 borrowed `fall` for hit, and the pack's own `die` is a 0.33 s topple) — while its idle, attack, crouch and landing read WORSE than the pack's hand-made ones: a human spine lean on a head-heavy chibi reads as a face-plant. So the set is the pack's own clips with the library's hit and death retargeted in. `shrink` still borrows `crouch`: the library's 44 clips have no shrink or cower either, and its Crouch_Idle_Loop face-plants on this rig. `block` still borrows `crouch` for the same reason.

experiment._what: `node tools/build-figures.mjs --clip-source experiment --out var/assets/figures/build/figures-ual.glb --no-manifest` builds the library with THIS map instead — every rig clip the library can supply, retargeted — which is how §3's comparison is reproduced.

scientist-chibi._role: Slices 1–3's body, kept as the CHIBI FALLBACK a traits.json row can ask for with "body": "chibi" (slice 4 — nothing lost). creature/subtype:scientist — Bold Biochemist, A.I.M. Scientists. Kenney's character-male-e: round glasses and a shirt-and-tie front with braces on the back — the one body in the kit that reads as a scientist face-on. Its head is the agent's shape, so from BEHIND it is told apart by the braces and by the lab tint; that is the trade, and it is written down.

drone._clips_note: There is no hit-react in this pack, and `hit` is deliberately ABSENT rather than borrowed: §3.6 rung 3 is that a missing clip removes only the part of the animation a model was going to add. The library's humanoid Hit_Chest was not retargeted onto it: an 11-joint flying robot has no legs, spine or neck for a humanoid clip to drive.
drone._triangles: Slice 4: decimated from 4,544 to the target by meshopt's simplifier — g1.jsonl@355 has three drones on the table, and the proportioned humans (and, since slice 4, the two duelists who stand in the same bodies) needed the triangles: the frame has to stay under report 13 §8.2's 30,000.

insect._role: Giant-Sized Flying Ant, Ant-Man's Air Force — creature/subtype:insect.
insect._clips_note: `summon` is absent — same rung-3 case as the drone's `hit`.
insect._triangles: Slice 4: decimated from 3,040 to the target, for the same budget.
